subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw solve this issue with a mutating restore/re-index command, a read-only archive/family-history API, or both?
rationale: The central user pain is real, but the permanent shape affects session-state semantics, archive retention, privacy boundaries, and whether recovery belongs in `openclaw doctor --fix`, a user command, or a read-only history surface.

options.title: Adopt Bounded Read Path First
options.body: Use the open `includeFamily` direction as the canonical retrieval path and add a narrow doctor/restore follow-up only for already-archived users who need mutation.

options.title: Add Explicit Restore Command
options.body: Build a guarded CLI/doctor recovery command that backs up state, restores selected archives, and rebuilds the session index with tests and migration guidance.

options.title: Keep As External Script
options.body: Leave archive mutation outside core and document manual recovery, accepting that non-technical users remain blocked without first-class recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Adopt Bounded Read Path First
recommendation.body: Use the open `includeFamily` direction as the canonical retrieval path and add a narrow doctor/restore follow-up only for already-archived users who need mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: They appear most connected to the current session/gateway history surfaces and the open family-history implementation path.
